sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Leon County?
sections.html:
Leon County splits the job in two: the Property Appraiser decides what a parcel is worth and who gets an exemption, and the Tax Collector prints the bills and takes the money. The Board of County Commissioners and other taxing bodies set the millage rates that connect the two.

The Tax Collector's own description of the sequence is simple. The appraiser assesses, the taxing bodies set rates, the appraiser builds the tax roll, and the roll is certified to the Tax Collector, who mails the notices. Name or address changes must go through the appraiser, because the Tax Collector cannot change the roll.

  • Leon County Property Appraiser: assessments, exemptions, parcel data, name and address updates.
  • Leon County Tax Collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent accounts, tax certificates.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: records deeds and collects document stamp tax at recording.

sections.h2: When is Leon County property tax billed, and when does it go delinquent?
sections.html:
Billing starts November 1 for the calendar year, and owners are held to know that tax is payable before April 1. The appraiser's office reported that the 2026 bills had been mailed in November.

On April 1 of the following year an unpaid bill becomes delinquent, and the Tax Collector adds a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, interest of 1.5 percent per month, and the statutory collection costs under s. 197.332(1). Within 45 days of delinquency the office must advertise a list of delinquent taxpayers in a local newspaper. Under the installment plan page, an amount unpaid on April 1 is also subject to a tax certificate on June 1.

Florida's early-payment scale of 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February applies here as everywhere. Owners who pay through a mortgage escrow should ask the lender to request the original notice so a copy reaches the owner.

sections.h2: Does Leon County offer an installment plan for property tax?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners whose estimated tax exceeds $100 can pay quarterly if the application reaches the Tax Collector before May 1, and the plan renews on its own each year once started.

The first payment is due by June 30 to earn the discount. A payment between June 30 and July 31 is accepted without a discount, and failing the first payment cancels enrollment, which leaves the full bill due by March 31. Once the June 30 deadline is met, the owner is bound to the plan for the whole year.

  • First installment, due by June 30: one quarter of the estimate, discounted 6 percent.
  • Second, due by September 30: discounted 4.5 percent.
  • Third, due by December 31: discounted 3 percent, with half of any adjustment to actual tax.
  • Fourth, due by March 31: no discount, with the rest of the adjustment.

The first two payments rest on the prior year's notice. A change in ownership, value or exemptions shows up in the third and fourth payments, so a seller who closes mid-year should tell the closing agent which installments are already paid.

sections.h2: What exemptions does the Leon County Property Appraiser list?
sections.html:
March 1 is the filing deadline for each tax year, and the appraiser's site covers homestead plus several veteran and service benefits. Homestead is the base for the other benefits listed, so owners should file for it first.

State law builds the homestead benefit in two layers: the first $25,000 of assessed value is exempt from all taxes, including school tax, and a further layer applies only to non-school taxes on value above $50,000. The owner must make the home a permanent residence by January 1, and the benefit ends if the home is rented or stops being the permanent home.

The veteran and military exemptions the office describes each require homestead first:

  • $5,000 off assessed value for a veteran with a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more, or a qualifying surviving spouse.
  • A tax discount for a veteran who is 65 or older with a combat-related disability, matched to the VA disability percentage.
  • Full exemption for a veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability, or a qualifying surviving spouse.
  • A deployed military exemption, applied for with Form DR-501M and a copy of deployment orders.

Documentation for these can go by email, mail, fax or in person. Florida lets counties and cities add senior exemptions with an income limit, so ask the appraiser which local ones apply to your address and what the current income limit is.

sections.h2: What caps and rules apply to Leon County assessments?
sections.html:
Non-homestead assessment growth is capped at 10 percent a year, and the appraiser says this cap applies to the non-school portion of value. Homestead assessed value is limited by Save Our Homes to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change.

Florida's published chart gives a 2.7 percent cap for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. A sale resets the property to just value on the next January 1, so a buyer of a long-held Leon County home often sees a higher assessment than the seller paid. That surprise is worth mentioning when you price a listing.

The appraiser's office also notes that Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027 and does not change 2026 bills. The office says it is waiting for state guidance, so check its site for anything that applies to the next roll.

sections.h2: What should a Leon County seller do about tax at closing?
sections.html:
Ask the title company for a tax proration and a payoff of anything delinquent, and confirm which installments are paid if you use the plan. Closing agents prorate the current year between buyer and seller, and any delinquent balance with interest is paid from your proceeds.

Document stamp tax on a Leon County deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the rate for every Florida county except Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk at the time of recording, and each party named in the document is liable however the parties split the cost.

Homestead does not pass to the buyer. They need their own application filed by the first of March, and if you buy another Florida home, portability of your Save Our Homes benefit uses Form DR-501T within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old homestead.

sections.h2: What does Leon County look like in the Census data?
sections.html:
Leon County, home to Tallahassee, had an estimated 299,048 people in the July 2025 estimate, across 668 square miles, and it is a renter-heavy market compared with most of Florida.

With just over half of homes owner-occupied, many Leon County sellers are investors with tenants in place. A rental is not eligible for homestead, and Florida's tenant notice rules apply to the sale timeline.

faqs.q: When does Leon County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year after the assessment. The Tax Collector then adds a delinquency fee, an advertising fee and 1.5 percent interest per month, plus statutory collection costs.

faqs.q: Can I pay Leon County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if estimated tax is above $100 and the application reaches the Tax Collector before May 1. Payments are due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three.

faqs.q: By when must Leon County homestead be filed?
faqs.a: The first of March. The appraiser accepts applications by email, mail, fax or in person. Ask the office for the current homestead amount.

faqs.q: Does Amendment 3 change my 2026 Leon County bill?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser's office states that Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027 and does not affect 2026 property tax bills.

faqs.q: Who changes the name or address on a Leon County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector. Updates to the roll must be processed by the appraiser, so call that office before the next bill is mailed.
